summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — DSFIR.AS +6%, EDV.L +6%, BAYN.DE +5%, DGE.L +4%, AAF.L +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CCH.L -19%, RHM.DE -18%, STMPA.PA -12%, IFX.DE -11%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: CCH.L (-18.73%) — Russia risk: Kommersant reported brewer Bochkari sought external management of Coca-Cola HBC's Russian units (Multon). The stock fell ~18% to about 4,050p even after a Q3 beat and raised guidance. Some reports date the drop to 5 Nov. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: CCH.L is a LSE-listed mid/large-cap consumer-staples bottler. The drop was a sudden geopolitical headline gap-down, so there was no pre-signal and a long-only bot would not short it.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news. Likely post-Q3 drift: Q3 trading update (~Nov 4) reportedly beat on fragrance-led core profit, and Citi raised its target to EUR 111. Unverified for Nov 6.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DSFIR.AS is a large-cap Dutch/Swiss flavours-and-fragrances name that no strategy includes. The move also looks like a follow-through gap after results, not a fresh same-day catalyst.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a uk-eu large-cap scan, e.g. Stoxx 600 names with a daily move ≥ +5% on ≥1.5× 20-day average volume, as a candidate list for momentum-trader. Also flag names within 3 days of an earnings date.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-06. Searches showed only routine buy-back notices, so this is likely a gold-price or sector-wide rally in LSE-listed gold miners.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EDV.L is a FTSE 100 gold miner with operations in West Africa, and no strategy lists it. With no company-specific news, a news-reactive bot had no trigger, and a +5.7% sector-beta move may not have cleared momentum thresholds.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EDV.L and similar LSE gold miners (e.g. FRES.L) to the commodity/momentum universe as a gold-beta sleeve, gated on a gold-futures daily move above a threshold such as +1.5%, so the next sector rally is caught.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver for 6 Nov. Bayer reported Q3 on about 3 Nov (narrower loss, raised FY guidance), so this is likely follow-through. A Roundup litigation headline is also possible but unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BAYN.DE is a large-cap German DAX pharma/agchem name, and no uk-eu strategy covers it. The move also followed a catalyst from days earlier, so a gap-up or news-reactive signal would not have fired today.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX/Euro Stoxx 50 constituents to the momentum universe, and add a post-earnings-drift rule: for 5 sessions after an earnings beat or guidance raise, allow entry on a close ≥ +3% on above-average volume (1.5× 20-day).

top_movers.catalyst: Diageo's Q1 trading update beat expectations (organic net sales about +1.4% vs consensus about -0.4%) and reiterated full-year guidance, pushing the shares to a 52-week high. Search dates were inconsistent, so the exact day is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DGE.L is a FTSE 100 consumer-staples large cap, and no strategy lists UK/EU staples. It was also a results-driven gap at the open, so a post-open momentum or news-reactive signal would have been late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 constituents to the news-reactive strategy's UK/EU universe, with a trading-update gate that releases names gapping ≥ +3% on ≥ 2× average volume within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-06. Airtel Africa's last confirmed news was the May 2026 Bharti Airtel stake move, so this looks like a technical rebound or buyback-supported move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AAF.L is a mid-cap FTSE 250 emerging-market telecom (Africa-focused, Bharti Airtel owns ~63%). Its modest +4.3% move with no news would not pass a catalyst or gap filter anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 250 names to the momentum universe, but only with a liquidity floor (e.g. 20-day average daily value ≥ £5M) and a ≥ +4% close-to-close trigger. Gate it on a confirmed RNS/news item so catalyst-free drifts like this stay excluded.

top_movers.catalyst: No dated news found for 2026-11-06. Likely a rebound in a stock down ~40% YTD, possibly lifted by European fintech/payments sentiment. Adyen raised 2026 growth guidance in August and announced an Orb acquisition.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ADYEN.AS is a large-cap Euronext Amsterdam fintech, and no strategy covers it. With no identifiable catalyst, a +3.8% move in a beaten-down name would also be a weak momentum signal and probably wouldn't pass a gap or volume filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap Euronext Amsterdam names (AEX constituents like ADYEN.AS) to the uk-eu momentum universe, with a gate requiring ≥1.5× 20-day average volume on a ≥+3% close, so ordinary rebounds don't trigger entries.

top_movers.catalyst: Russia risk: Kommersant reported brewer Bochkari sought external management of Coca-Cola HBC's Russian units (Multon). The stock fell ~18% to about 4,050p even after a Q3 beat and raised guidance. Some reports date the drop to 5 Nov.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CCH.L is a LSE-listed mid/large-cap consumer-staples bottler. The drop was a sudden geopolitical headline gap-down, so there was no pre-signal and a long-only bot would not short it.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for the long-only constraint. If the universe is widened, add a FTSE 100/250 staples watchlist with a headline-risk flag (e.g. 'Russia' keyword on a held name) that triggers a cut-exposure check, not a new entry.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 results missed (revenue €3.15B vs €3.23B est, adj. EPS 7% below consensus) and Rheinmetall cut its 2026 sales guidance to about €13.2B from €13.7–14.2B on Boxer and artillery-ammo delays.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: RHM.DE is a German large-cap defence name that no strategy covers. The drop was also a scheduled-earnings gap-down, and a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot has no short leg to act on it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add European defence large-caps (RHM.DE, BA.L, HO.FP) to a watchlist universe. Give the earnings-gate a post-results gap-down ≤-10% rule that flags the name for mean-reversion review after a 1–2 session cool-off, not for entry on the day.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed news for 2026-11-06. Searches only found the 23 Jul 2026 Q3 guidance-miss sell-off, so today's -11.7% is probably an unconfirmed semis/auto-chip sector move or a follow-on from that.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: STMPA.PA is a large-cap Euronext Paris listing of a European semiconductor name that no uk-eu strategy covers. A drop this size was also a long-only bot's wrong side, with no obvious bounce setup.
top_movers.suggestion: Add STMPA.PA and similar large-cap EU semis (ASML, Infineon) to the mean-reversion universe, with a filter that waits for a one-day drop of at least 8% on above-average volume (1.5× the 20-day average) and then a stabilisation day.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst found for the -11.41% drop. Searches turned up nothing dated 6 Nov 2026. The likely cause is a sector-wide semiconductor/AI-chip sell-off, or a pre-results de-rating ahead of Q4 results due about 10–12 Nov.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: IFX.DE is a large-cap German (Xetra) semiconductor, and no uk-eu strategy includes it. With no clear news trigger, a news-reactive filter would have had nothing to fire on. The bot also can't short.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU semis (IFX.DE, STM.PA, ASML.AS) to the mean-reversion watchlist. Flag any ≥-8% single-day drop with no news hit as a candidate for next-day rebound entry, with a volume floor of 1.5× the 20-day average.
